title: Operator-prioritization queue and guided failover runbook for multiregion inference
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Create an operator-focused runbook and automation to reduce pager noise while enabling safe, observable multiregion failover and controlled load shedding. This work bundles: (1) a priority bucketing / operator queue for alerts so on-call sees a concise, actionable list; (2) automated circuit-breaker triggers that gracefully degrade noncritical paths and shed load when cluster capacity is constrained; (3) a guided failover playbook for shifting traffic across regions with cache-rewarm and KV-consistency checks; (4) pager suppression and escalation rules tied to SLO context so we avoid noisy, low-signal alerts during known transient degradations.
acceptance_criteria: Prioritization queue prototype deployed to staging and visible in the Console; alerts classified into 3 operator buckets (Actionable, Investigate, FYI)

Circuit-breaker policy implemented for text-generation serving that (a) trips after >=30% sustained p99 latency regression for 5m or >=15% 5xx rate for 3m; (b) triggers automated graceful degradation for noncritical endpoints (caching, embeddings precompute) reducing token throughput by target 30%
Pager suppression rules added: transient SLO-warning alerts suppressed for 10 minutes if correlated region-level load spike is detected and fallback region healthy
Guided failover runbook published (Confluence link) with scriptable steps, verification checks (end-to-end latency, KV cache hit rate, sample inference correctness), and rollback criteria
Automated integration tests (chaos + synthetic load) exercising load-shedding and failover in staging with postmortem template wired to the alert
Runbook reviewed and approved by SRE, Platform, and Product (signoffs in PRD)
Downtime / customer-impact play path documented and drills scheduled in Cycle 2026-W12
updates: 2026-03-05: Ticket created. Problem statement derived from two incidents in Feb where noisy region-level alerts caused on-call thrash and delayed failover decision (INC-2026-02-18, INC-2026-02-26).

2026-03-06: Design spike completed. Decided on 3 operator buckets and a lightweight prioritization queue surfaced in Console; will reuse existing alert fingerprinting pipeline (ENG-8721) and the new SLO-context enrichment service (ENG-91234).

2026-03-08: Prototype circuit-breaker thresholds chosen after historical analysis: trip if p99 latency > target * 1.3 for 5m or 5xx rate delta >= +15% for 3m. Trade-offs: aggressive thresholds reduce customer errors faster but risk unnecessary shedding; mitigation is canaryed rollout + dynamic hysteresis (exponential backoff).

2026-03-09: Implemented initial pager suppression rules in staging: correlate region CPU/GPU utilization and increase page-suppression TTL to 10m when a correlated surge is detected. Observability hooks added to track suppressed vs fired alerts (dashboards: https://metrics.redwood.ai/d/regional/alert-suppression).

2026-03-10: Draft runbook created (Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RR/Operator+Prioritization+and+Failover+Runbook). Includes step-by-step guided actions: triage, decide failover, execute traffic shift, cache rewarm, verify, and postmortem checklist. Shared with SRE for feedback.

2026-03-11: PR opened for automation and policy (GitHub: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/4278). Contains Lambda to toggle circuit-breaker thresholds, orchestration for progressive load-shed, and Slack-driven guided runbook integration. Requesting review from @sre-team and @platform-owners.

2026-03-12: Feedback from Platform (Marco Chen): add explicit KV-consistency verification step after failover and require automated smoke tests (10 sample prompts) before marking failover done. Also strong recommendation to surface approximate rollback cost estimate in Console (tokens/min lost) before operator confirms failover.

Run staging chaos exercise (cross-region failover under high KV-miss) and capture metrics — schedule 2026-03-16
Enable limited canary of suppression + circuit-breaker policies for 10% of production traffic (region eu-west-1) after staging signoff
Organize a 1-hour on-call drill during Cycle 2026-W12 and record runbook timing/observability gaps
